title: Backups become readable: a durable per-backup restore-proof record in three states, served over HTTP
description:
PREREQUISITE ROW spun out of task-df972c274f2a43eda3a9f57d2780c6f9 (the Environments surface) by worker-b1872f24 on 2026-09-07, which is BLOCKED on it. Parent id: task-df972c274f2a43eda3a9f57d2780c6f9.

THE GAP, MEASURED ON DISK, NOT INFERRED. The parent's DoD 3 requires a backups list rendering RESTORE-PROOF state in three values. NOTHING IS SERVED, and there is nothing to decode:
 - `apps/daemon/src/backups/scheduled-backup.ts` computes the fact: `ScheduledBackupResult.status: "VERIFIED" | "FAILED"` (:21), `sha256: string | null` (:23), `proof: BackupProof | null` (:24), inside a `ScheduledBackupReceipt` (:28-33). That is task-95e68a8d's restore-to-temp sha256 proof.
 - `grep -rn "scheduled-backup" apps/daemon/src` OUTSIDE `apps/daemon/src/backups/` returns ZERO. No importer. No port. No composition edge.
 - The served read roster (apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:78-110) has NO backups route. `/activation/read` mentions backups only to state it DEFERS taking one (activation-read.ts:7-10,146-155).
So the receipt is computed and then reaches nothing. This is the classic producer with no consumer edge: it satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

TWO VALUES ARE NOT THREE. `status` is `"VERIFIED" | "FAILED"`. The parent's DoD needs proven / failed / NOT YET CHECKED as three distinct values, and NOT-YET-CHECKED must never render as proven - that collapse is the whole failure this surface exists to prevent, because an operator leans on the difference at the worst possible moment. A backup that was WRITTEN but whose restore check has not run is a real, common state (the check is expensive and the write is not), and today the type cannot express it. Decide where the third value comes from - a durable record with no proof row yet, or an explicit third member - and make it impossible to默 default into VERIFIED.

WHAT THIS ROW OWES, in build order:
 1. DURABILITY. `runScheduledBackup` returns a receipt to its caller and nothing persists it. A read route needs a durable record keyed by backup ref, carrying the restore-proof state, the sha256 when there is one, and when the check last ran. Measure first whether a store already holds it before adding one.
 2. THE PORT AND THE ROUTE. A `/backups/read` (or equivalent) in the served roster. Note from task-509c6c16's handoff that composition for a daemon read route is SIX files, not four: the route module + `.js` bridge + test, `http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` (five edits: import, JSON_ROUTES roster, serve fn, method guard, dispatch branch), `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts` (five edits: factory type, Resolved field, FACTORIES roster, validation block, spread), and `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` + `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` for the store-backed port. `daemon-entry-ops.test.ts:187` spells the chain out.
 3. THE ROSTER BACKFILLS a new read route owes, invisible to targeted runs and only found by `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`: `http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` roster.size pin, UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS and UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES (each needs a comment naming this row and the consumer that retires it - a separate arm greps those comments); and the EXACT `providerKeys` list in `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`.
 4. THE CONSUMER EDGE, so this row does not repeat the gap it exists to close: the `dev-proxy-paths.ts` pin, an exact-key client decoder beside apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts, and the backups list rendered in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx - which is already wired into the Health screen through live-environments.tsx and LiveHealth. Retire both census entries in the same edit. If that breaches this row's file ceiling, SPLIT the browser half into its own row and name it in dependsOn rather than shipping a route nothing fetches.

A SECRET NEVER SURFACES (epic rail 3). Backup refs and connection strings are adjacent here; task-95e68a8d already established that connection strings are never serialised on a failure path. Carry the ref and the sha256, never a credential, and never a raw path that leaks one.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` AND `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
definitionOfDone: A durable per-backup record exists carrying restore-proof state in THREE distinct values - proven / failed / not yet checked - plus the sha256 when there is one and when the check last ran. Assert the three are distinct by VALUE at the store seam, and assert a record written WITHOUT a restore check reads as not-yet-checked and NOT as proven. Mutate the mapping so not-yet-checked returns proven and show the arm reds; a test that only counts records passes that mutation.

The state is served over HTTP on a route in the JSON_ROUTES roster, composed into the PRODUCTION listener, and reached through it in a test - not only at the handler seam. Refusals fail closed with stable codes and a rostered layer; assert the specific code, not merely that it did not succeed.

Every roster backfill a new read route owes is done and green under `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`: the http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts roster.size pin, UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS and UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES with a comment naming this row and its retiring consumer, and the exact providerKeys list in daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts. A targeted run does not find these.

THE CONSUMER EDGE EXISTS, not just the export: the dev-proxy-paths.ts pin, an exact-key client decoder refusing an extra key AND a missing key with the code asserted, and the backups list rendered in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx with the state in a data- attribute and the three visually distinguishable by more than colour. The two census entries are retired in the same edit. If this breaches the file ceiling, split the browser half into its own row named in dependsOn - do not ship a route nothing fetches.

The browser arms assert the three states SEPARATELY and assert specifically that not-yet-checked does NOT render as proven. Drill it: render not-yet-checked the same as proven and show the arm reds by VALUE, not by a row count. Quote the drill outcome with a restore proof.
No secret, credential or connection string reaches the record, the frame, a log line, an error path or a committed fixture. Assert a failure path serialises no connection string.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A bare `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file and is not evidence here.
taskRails: THREE VALUES, NEVER TWO. `ScheduledBackupResult.status` is VERIFIED|FAILED today. Not-yet-checked must be expressible and must never default into proven - that collapse is the entire failure this surface exists to prevent.

A PRODUCER WITH NO CONSUMER EDGE IS THE GAP THIS ROW EXISTS TO CLOSE. scheduled-backup.ts has zero importers outside its own directory; do not repeat that shape. Land the consumer edge or name the row that does, in dependsOn.
A DAEMON READ ROUTE IS SIX FILES OF COMPOSITION, not four, plus four roster backfills only `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` finds. See task-509c6c16.
A SECRET NEVER SURFACES IN PLAINTEXT (epic rail 3) - not in the record, the frame, a log line, an error path or a committed fixture.
ANYTHING THIS ROW STARTS, IT STOPS (epic rail 4). A restore check that spins up a disposable database owns its teardown on EVERY exit path, including the failure ones.
ASCII-ONLY SOURCES, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT, EXACT-KEY decoders, dev-proxy-paths pin for any new read.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. The row description's measurements are good; three of them need correcting or confirming before you build:
(a) CONFIRM THE GAP: `git grep -n 'scheduled-backup\|runScheduledBackup' -- 'apps/**' 'packages/**' ':!apps/daemon/src/backups/*' ':!*.js'` returns ZERO at my HEAD. The receipt is computed and reaches nothing. If that has changed, STOP AND REPORT — someone else has landed a consumer.
(b) **THE DESCRIPTION UNDERCOUNTS THE COMPOSITION.** It says a read route is six files. `git show --stat 29f5d723` — task-509c6c16's `/deployments/health/read`, the landed precedent — touched FIFTEEN source files for the daemon half alone. Read that commit before writing anything: it is your template, and copying it is cheaper and safer than rediscovering the chain. The three one-line edits are easy to miss: `daemon-entry.ts:321` (conditional spread of the resolved port into the listener options), `daemon-store-dependencies.ts:132` (the provider thunk that throws "unreachable: the ... is always wired"), and `http-listener.ts:165` (the optional port on `StartListenerOptions`, with a comment saying what ABSENT means — the precedent's comment is the model: absent must refuse as UNAVAILABLE, never answer a healthy default).
(c) `sed -n '17,33p' apps/daemon/src/backups/scheduled-backup.ts` — `ScheduledBackupResult` is `{environment, kind, status: "VERIFIED"|"FAILED", ref, sha256: string|null, proof: BackupProof|null, failure, stage}` inside `ScheduledBackupReceipt` (:28-33). TWO values, and `apps/daemon/src/backups/` holds only `backup-ports` and `scheduled-backup` — no store, no record, nothing persists the receipt.
(d) THE CENSUS ROSTERS you must backfill live in ONE file: `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` — `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` at :129 (currently EMPTY), `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` at :174, asserted by `toStrictEqual` at :456 and :481, and a comment-grep arm at :505. `JSON_ROUTES` is at http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:77-110 (37 members today).
BASELINE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line. It is slow (~22 min) and flaky on this branch; you need it because this row edits eighteen files and you must be able to tell your red from a peer's.

THE THREE-STATE DURABLE RECORD (DoD 1), ARMS FIRST. New module `apps/daemon/src/backups/backup-restore-proof.ts` plus its one-line tracked bridge `backup-restore-proof.js` (`export * from "./backup-restore-proof.ts";` — every runtime module in this tree has one) and `backup-restore-proof.test.ts`.
**THE DESIGN DECISION THIS ROW OWES, MADE: AN EXPLICIT THIRD MEMBER IN A NEW VOCABULARY, NOT A WIDENED `status`.** The record carries `restoreProof: "PROVEN" | "FAILED" | "NOT_CHECKED"`. Do NOT widen `ScheduledBackupResult.status` — it is the backup RUN's own outcome and belongs to task-95e68a8d (DONE); widening it changes a landed contract and drags that row's arms in. The record is a new durable projection with its own three-value vocabulary.
**MAKE PROVEN UNREACHABLE BY DEFAULT** (task rail 1). The mapping from a receipt result is TOTAL and EXPLICIT: `VERIFIED` -> PROVEN, `FAILED` -> FAILED, and a record written with no restore check -> NOT_CHECKED. Write it as an exhaustive switch with NO `default:` branch and no `??`/`||` fallback, so a fourth input is a TYPE ERROR rather than a silent PROVEN. The state field is REQUIRED on the type, never optional — an optional field is one `?? "PROVEN"` away from the collapse this row exists to prevent.
THE RECORD ALSO CARRIES: the backup `ref` (the key), `sha256: string | null` — null exactly when there is no proof — and `checkedAt: string | null` (when the restore check last ran), null when it has not. Absent is NULL, never an empty string and never a zero.
ARMS, red first:
(a) **THE THREE ARE DISTINCT BY VALUE at the store seam** — write three records and read back three different `restoreProof` values. Not a count.
(b) **A RECORD WRITTEN WITHOUT A RESTORE CHECK READS AS NOT_CHECKED, NOT PROVEN**, with `sha256: null` and `checkedAt: null`.
(c) **REFUSALS FAIL CLOSED** with a stable code AND a rostered layer — an unreadable store, a malformed stored row, an unknown ref. Assert the specific code and layer, never merely that it did not succeed (global rail 1).
(d) **NO SECRET REACHES THE RECORD** (DoD 6, epic rail 3): a failure path serialises no connection string and no raw path that leaks one. Assert on the FAILURE path, with a positive control over a literal containing a connection-string shape so the arm cannot pass vacuously.
MEASURE FIRST whether an existing store already holds per-backup rows before adding a new one — the description asks for that check and it is cheaper than a second store.

PERSIST THE RECEIPT (DoD 1) — `apps/daemon/src/backups/scheduled-backup.ts` and `scheduled-backup.test.ts`. This is the edge that closes the producer-with-no-consumer gap on the WRITE side; step 5 closes it on the READ side.
`runScheduledBackup` returns a `ScheduledBackupReceipt` to its caller and nothing persists it. Write one record per `ScheduledBackupResult` through step 2's module, keyed by `ref`, mapping `status` through the exhaustive mapper — never by re-deriving the state here, or there are two mappings to keep in step.
**DO NOT CHANGE `ScheduledBackupResult`, `ScheduledBackupReceipt` OR THE RUN'S BEHAVIOUR.** Add persistence at the seam and nothing else: this function is task-95e68a8d's delivered surface, it is DONE, and its arms pin its shape. If persisting forces a signature change, keep it ADDITIVE (an optional port parameter, absent in existing callers) and say so.
**THE WRITE OWNS ITS TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH INCLUDING THE FAILURE ONES** (task rail 5, epic rail 4). This function already spins up and tears down temp directories for the restore check; a persistence failure must not leak one. Assert teardown on the failure path, not only the success path.
ARMS: a run whose restore check VERIFIED persists PROVEN with its sha256; a run that FAILED persists FAILED; a `skipped` environment (`DATABASE_ABSENT`) persists nothing at all rather than a NOT_CHECKED row that would later read as a backup nobody took — or, if you decide it SHOULD persist, say why in a comment at the site. Assert the persisted values by reading them back through step 2's reader, not through the writer's return value.

THE ROUTE MODULE (DoD 2) — new `apps/daemon/src/http/backups-read.ts`, its one-line tracked bridge `backups-read.js`, and `backups-read.test.ts`. COPY `apps/daemon/src/http/deployments-health-read.ts` (251 lines, landed by task-509c6c16 in 29f5d723) as the shape: the port type, the refusal vocabulary, the frame assembly and the fail-closed default all follow it.
THE FRAME carries, per backup: `ref`, `restoreProof` in the three values, `sha256` (null when absent) and `checkedAt` (null when absent). Nothing else — no path, no connection string, no credential (DoD 6, task rail 4). Export the path constant (`BACKUPS_READ_PATH`) beside its siblings so step 5 can roster it.
**ABSENT PORT REFUSES AS UNAVAILABLE, NEVER ANSWERS A DEFAULT.** The precedent's comment at http-listener.ts:165 states the principle for its own route: a daemon composed without the port cannot see anything, and answering a healthy default is the most dangerous output such a route has. The same holds here and more sharply — answering PROVEN for a backup nobody checked is exactly the collapse task rail 1 forbids.
ARMS in `backups-read.test.ts`: the three states each served BY VALUE; an unreadable store refuses with its specific code AND layer; a record with no sha256 and no checkedAt serves nulls rather than empty strings; and a failure path serialises no connection string, with a positive control. These are handler-seam arms — step 7 is what proves the route is reachable through the production listener, and DoD 2 requires both.

THE COMPOSITION CHAIN (DoD 2) — six files, all of them small, and the row's highest risk of a silent omission because a missed link fails as a 404 rather than a compile error. Follow `git show 29f5d723` link for link:
1. `http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` — FIVE edits: the import, the `JSON_ROUTES` roster entry (:77-110), the serve function, the method guard, and the dispatch branch. The file's own header comment explains why the chain's final `else` stays unconditional; do not turn it into a branch.
2. `http/http-listener-guards.ts` — the method guard entry.
3. `http/http-listener.ts` — the optional port on `StartListenerOptions` (~:165), WITH a comment stating what ABSENT means, following the precedent's wording.
4. `daemon-entry-port-resolution.ts` — FIVE edits: the factory type, the `Resolved` field, the `FACTORIES` roster, the validation block, and the spread.
5. `daemon-entry.ts` — the conditional spread of the resolved port into the listener options (~:321). Conditional, never an assigned `undefined`.
6. `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts` — the store-backed port, built from step 2's reader. This file is edited by several rows: add the port and nothing else, no refactor.
7. `daemon-store-dependencies.ts` — the provider thunk (~:132), including the `throw new Error("unreachable: the ... is always wired")` guard the siblings all carry.
Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` scoped to the dispatch and entry tests after this step if you can; the full leg is step 8.

THE ROSTER BACKFILLS (DoD 3) — invisible to a targeted run; ONLY `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` finds them, which is why they are their own step.
In `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts`:
(a) the `roster.size` pin — one more served path;
(b) `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` (:129, currently an EMPTY frozen array, asserted by `toStrictEqual` at :456) — add this route's path;
(c) `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` (:174, asserted at :481) — add it, **with a comment naming THIS ROW (task-1f994315fd) and the consumer that retires it: task-679cdaa380874f55978e8790d770e37a**, the browser child I filed for the Health-screen backups list. A separate arm at :505 GREPS those comments, so a bare entry without the comment reds.
In `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`: the EXACT `providerKeys` list gains the new provider.
BOTH CENSUS ENTRIES ARE DELIBERATE AND TEMPORARY. They record, in the daemon's own tests, that this route is served but not yet fetched — which is the honest state until task-679cdaa3 lands, and is how this board keeps a producer-with-no-consumer visible instead of silent (task rail 2). Retiring them is that row's DoD 5, not yours. Do NOT pre-retire them, and do NOT skip them to avoid the census: an unrostered served path reds the bidirectional roster arm.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your own diff as an attacker first.
DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST and record the output. SIX of this row's files are NEW and therefore UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to them and certifies nothing: back each up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13). The tracked files take an empty `git diff -- <path>` in a separate call. State which paths fell in which class.
THREE DRILLS, each quoted with its failing line:
(i) **THE ROW'S ONE SAFETY PROPERTY** (DoD 1): change the mapper so a record with no restore check yields PROVEN. Confirm step 2's arm (b) AND step 7's arm (b) both go RED. If only the store arm reds, the wire is untested for the collapse and step 7 must be strengthened — that is the whole point of having both.
(ii) **THE COMPOSITION DRILL**: remove the dispatch branch (or the `JSON_ROUTES` entry) and confirm step 7 reds with a 404 rather than passing. A route that only works at the handler seam is the failure DoD 2's second half exists to catch.
(iii) **THE SECRET DRILL** (DoD 6): make a failure path include the connection string. Confirm the arm reds — and check it reds on the VALUE, not merely on a changed message length.
GATES — standalone and foreground, ONE command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line, because an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, then `pnpm typecheck`. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is NOT required by this row — the browser half is task-679cdaa3 — but the row's DoD 7 names it, so run it if it is cheap and say plainly that this row touches no control-room file either way. A bare root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file; say that rather than quoting it. The daemon leg is slow (~22 min) and flaky here: attribute any red outside this row's eighteen files against your step 1 baseline and disclose foreign red verbatim rather than owning it or calling it green.
SELF-REVIEW AND RECORD, in completionSummary plus one row comment for detail over the cap: the three-state vocabulary and WHY it is a new member rather than a widened `ScheduledBackupResult.status`; that the mapper is an exhaustive switch with no default so PROVEN is unreachable by fallback; every link of the composition chain, named, so a reviewer can check none was skipped; the two census entries with the comment naming task-679cdaa3; the three drill outcomes with their failing lines; and that DoD 4 and DoD 5 are delivered by task-679cdaa380874f55978e8790d770e37a, which dependsOn this row — this row deliberately lands a served route that nothing fetches yet, recorded as such in the daemon's own census rather than hidden. Named verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.

EIGHTEEN IS OVER TARGET AND I AM NOT SPLITTING FURTHER, deliberately. The next seam would put the durable record in its own row - and that row would be a producer with no consumer, which is exactly the shape rail 2 forbids. The record plus the route is one idea: a fact computed, persisted and served. The precedent shipped fifteen files as one reviewable row on this board. Flagging the count rather than hiding it.

THE DESIGN DECISION THE ROW OWED, MADE: AN EXPLICIT THIRD MEMBER IN A NEW VOCABULARY. The record carries `restoreProof: "PROVEN" | "FAILED" | "NOT_CHECKED"`. NOT a widened `ScheduledBackupResult.status`, for three reasons: that shape is task-95e68a8d's delivered contract and it is DONE with arms pinning it; `status` answers the backup RUN's outcome, a different question from "has this backup been proven restorable", and one field answering two questions is how they collapse; and a new record can make the state REQUIRED, where a reused optional field is always one `?? AND THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THE COLLAPSE UNREACHABLE RATHER THAN MERELY DISCOURAGED: the receipt-to-record mapping is an EXHAUSTIVE SWITCH WITH NO `default:` BRANCH and no `??`/`||` fallback, so an unhandled input is a TYPE ERROR at build time instead of a silent PROVEN at runtime. Drill (i) mutates it and requires BOTH the store-seam arm and the through-the-listener arm to red - if only the store arm reds, the wire is untested for the collapse and the entry test must be strengthened.

REJECTED - deriving the third state from the ABSENCE of a record. "No row yet" and NOT_CHECKED would then be one observation, and the route could not tell a backup nobody has checked from a ref that does not exist. Those must stay apart; answering the same for both is the second-worst output after a false PROVEN.

THE CENSUS ENTRIES ARE DELIBERATE AND TEMPORARY. Step 6 adds this route to UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS (http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:129, currently an empty frozen array) and to UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES (:174) WITH a comment naming this row and task-679cdaa3 as the consumer that retires it - the arm at :505 greps those comments, so a bare entry reds. That records, in the daemon's own tests, that the route is served and not yet fetched: the honest state until the browser row lands, and how this board keeps a producer-with-no-consumer visible instead of silent. Retiring them is that row's DoD 5, not this one's.
